Container.Name: media-audit
Container.Overview: Scans your media library (read-only) and reports what's actually in it: size per movie, show and season (with average episode size), and the container, codecs, resolution, HDR10/HDR10+/Dolby Vision, Atmos/DTS:X, audio and subtitle languages and release group of every file. An Issues page lists unreadable files, duplicate episodes and movie versions (with the space they use), stray and orphaned files, runtime and bitrate outliers, missing episodes and naming problems.[br][br]The container keeps running: it serves the web UI on port 8484 (click the container icon, then WebUI) and rescans on a schedule (03:00 daily by default; change it under Settings → Scanning); the Scans page has a Scan now button. Rescans only re-read new or changed files.[br][br]On the very first start it writes /config/config.yml from the folders it finds under /media and does not scan until you press Scan now, so you can review the library list first. The web UI has no login; keep it on your LAN.
Container.Changes:
### 0.8.1 - The Scan schedule, Scan workers and Host appdata path container variables are gone: set them in the web UI under Settings (Scanning, and General → Cleanup scripts). Remove them from an existing container (Edit, then remove the three variables) so they stop overriding the settings.
### 0.8.0 - Settings page: set up everything from the web UI (libraries with a folder browser, scanning, schedule, linking, languages, Issues checks, media folders and server paths) without editing config.yml.
### 0.7.0 - Libraries can live in several media folders or mounts (mount each under /media); path mappings tell cleanup scripts where each one is on the server. - Everything about a library's files is stored relative to the library, so renaming or moving a library never re-reads it. The database is upgraded on first start (backed up first). - New command-line tools to change libraries and path mappings without editing config.yml by hand.
### 0.6.0 - Renamed or moved library folders: the Scans page spots them and remaps the library (config.yml included), keeping its history and analysis instead of reading everything again. - Files page: multi-select filters with Is / Is not, live counts, subtitle language, group by title or season.
### 0.5.0 - Issues: .nfo files media servers don't read (scene release info, leftovers from moved episodes) are now stray files, so cleanup scripts quarantine them. New info check for episodes sitting outside their season folder. - Cleanup scripts: the Issues page writes a script (saved to appdata, or downloaded) that moves junk files to a quarantine folder and removes empty folders. You review and run it; media-audit stays read-only. Set the new Host media path variable to the same folder as Media.
### 0.4.0 - Files page: the grey folder line under each file name lists every file in that folder. - Titles page: the issue count now follows the season count. - Issues: new folder checks: seasons split across folders (Season 1 + Season 01), folders with no videos left, and empty folders. - Template: icon, updated description.
### 0.3.0 - Web UI (Overview, Titles, Files, Issues, Scans) and scheduled scans; the container now stays running. - Issues page: problems, duplicates, outliers and naming checks, with an Ignore button. - Average episode size per show and season.

Config.Name: Config
Config.Description: Config file and SQLite database. Keep this on the cache/appdata share, not on the media array.

Config.Name: Media
Config.Description: Folder containing your libraries (e.g. movies/, tv/). Mounted read-only; media-audit never modifies files.

Config.Name: PUID
Config.Description: User ID the scanner runs as (99 = nobody).

Config.Name: PGID
Config.Description: Group ID the scanner runs as (100 = users).

Config.Name: Host media path (cleanup scripts)
Config.Description: Set this to the same folder as Media above. Cleanup scripts (Issues page) run on the server, not in the container, and use it to find your libraries. If you add more media paths (mount them under /media, e.g. /media/archive), add a path mapping for each: see the README. media-audit itself never writes to your media.
